# Prohibited Practices

The following are never allowed in any environment that can reach production. Each item points to the policy card that explains the safe alternative.

- P-01 Hardcoding credentials, API keys, tokens or connection strings in source code. See SCS-SEC-01. Source: IT-57 §10 #1.
- P-02 Committing secrets, certificates, private keys or signing keystores to Git repositories. See SCS-SEC-01, SCS-SEC-03. Source: IT-57 §10 #2.
- P-03 Using string concatenation or interpolation to build SQL queries with user-supplied input. See SCS-INP-02, SCS-DB-01. Source: IT-57 §10 #3.
- P-04 Disabling HTTPS, certificate validation (for example badCertificateCallback returning true or TrustServerCertificate=True) or security middleware in production. See SCS-CRY-01, SCS-WEB-01. Source: IT-57 §10 #4.
- P-05 Exposing stack traces, internal paths or system details in API error responses or error screens. See SCS-ERR-01. Source: IT-57 §10 #5.
- P-07 Using wildcard CORS policies (AllowAnyOrigin, WithOrigins("*"), or any origin with credentials) in production. See SCS-API-04. Source: IT-57 §10 #7.
- P-08 Deploying code to production without the Security Reviewer's final approval, or deploying a version other than the one approved. See SCS-DEP-01, SCS-TEST-04. Source: IT-57 §10 #8; IT-29 §9.6.
- P-09 Logging passwords, tokens, personal data or full payment card numbers. See SCS-LOG-02. Source: IT-57 §10 #9.
- P-10 Using deprecated or known-vulnerable libraries without a documented risk acceptance. See SCS-SUP-01, SCS-SUP-02. Source: IT-57 §10 #10.
- P-11 Using sa, root, db_owner or other admin database accounts for application connections. See SCS-DB-02. Source: IT-57 §10 #11.
- P-12 Leaving debug mode, test accounts or development endpoints active in production. See SCS-DEP-03, SCS-AUTH-06. Source: IT-57 §10 #12.
- P-13 Relying on client-side checks (hidden buttons, route guards, app-side validation) as the only security control. See SCS-AUTHZ-01, SCS-INP-01. Source: New: OWASP Top 10 A01, MASVS.
- P-14 Loading or changing a record by ID without checking that the caller may access it. See SCS-AUTHZ-02. Source: New: OWASP API Security Top 10 API1.
- P-15 Binding request bodies directly to database entities, or returning entities from APIs. See SCS-API-02. Source: New: OWASP API Security Top 10 API3.
- P-16 Shipping privileged API keys or secrets inside the mobile app, web bundle, --dart-define values or a bundled .env file. See SCS-SEC-01. Source: New: OWASP Mobile Top 10 M1.
- P-18 Using MD5, SHA-1, DES/3DES, ECB mode or System.Random / Random() for security purposes, or storing passwords in plain text or reversibly encrypted. See SCS-CRY-02, SCS-AUTH-02. Source: New: OWASP Top 10 A04; IT-57 §8 Data Protection.
- P-19 Using BinaryFormatter, Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling other than None, or other serializers that let the payload choose the type. See SCS-INP-05. Source: New: OWASP Top 10 A08.
- P-20 Sending secrets, tokens or personal data in URL query strings. See SCS-SEC-01, SCS-LOG-02. Source: New: OWASP ASVS V14.2.
- P-21 Swallowing exceptions with empty catch blocks, or allowing access when a security check throws. See SCS-ERR-02. Source: New: OWASP Top 10 A10.
- P-22 Acting as Security Reviewer for, or approving, code you wrote yourself. See SCS-TEST-03. Source: New: ISO 27001 A.5.3 / NIST AC-5 separation of duties.
